author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces
summary: Both vet directory surfaces accept an optional specialty narrowing: the HTML page (REQ-VET-001) and the reinstated machine-readable surface (REQ-VET-003). Matching is whole-name and case-insensitive; a blank value is treated as absent; an unmatched value yields the directory with no veterinarians and a normal response; paging preserves the narrowing.
acceptance_criteria: HTML directory narrowed to a held specialty lists only those veterinarians, with paging applied to the narrowed list
narrowing matches a specialty name whole and case-insensitively; a partial name does not match
a narrowing naming no held specialty yields the directory with no veterinarians and a normal, non-error response
a blank or all-spaces narrowing behaves as though no narrowing were given, on both surfaces
moving to a later page of a filtered HTML directory keeps the narrowing applied
the machine-readable surface carries the same veterinarians and specialties as the page, and accepts the same specialty narrowing with identical matching and empty-result behavior
without a narrowing, both surfaces behave as before
non_goals: no visible form, dropdown, or other page control for the filter (URL contract only)
no free-text veterinarian search (NG-9 stays for typed-name search); REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused
notes: Slice spans two requirements: the HTML filter folds into REQ-VET-001 and the reinstated machine-readable surface is the fresh REQ-VET-003; both share one matcher. Non-goal narrowing recorded in adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. The adr/README.md index still needs the new ADR row added by system-design-expert/doc-sync (outside product-requirements-expert write scope).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice applies the established owner search+paging pattern to the vet feature; no new module, pattern, or integration. It stays inside the vet feature package under the controller-direct-to-repository shape (system-design Overview, Package Structure). The HTML surface mirrors OwnerController.processFindForm (blank-as-broadest search, strip normalization) and OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith (derived paged filter); the difference is a whole-name case-insensitive equality match traversing the Vet.specialties ManyToMany rather than a lastName prefix. The /vets route already exists (system-design Contracts, VetController) and gains the same optional parameter. Both surfaces share one matcher by delegating the match to the repository query. Basis: Read of OwnerController.java, VetController.java, VetRepository.java, Vet.java, vetList.html, ownersList.html; IntelliJ oracle not available this run (weaker, grep/Read basis).
integration_points: VetRepository gains specialty-filtered finders: a paged finder for /vets.html and an unpaged Collection finder for /vets. Push the whole-name case-insensitive match into the query (derived IgnoreCase equality traversing the specialties collection, or an equivalent JPQL join) rather than filtering in memory — this is the single shared matcher and keeps data access parameterized.

VetController normalizes the specialty parameter once (strip; null/blank/all-spaces -> no narrowing) mirroring OwnerController.processFindForm, and routes the absent/blank case to the existing findAll methods so unfiltered behavior and cache entries are byte-for-byte preserved.
VetController passes the normalized specialty back into the model so vetList.html can append it to every pagination link; the /vets JSON handler applies the same filter and wraps the result in Vets.

patterns.description: processFindForm: blank-as-broadest-search with strip normalization — the template for the specialty blank/absent handling
findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable): derived paged filter finder — the shape the specialty-filtered finder follows, swapping StartingWith prefix for IgnoreCase whole-name equality

risks.risk: @Cacheable("vets") is on both findAll() and findAll(Pageable); a new filtered finder shares the same cache name
risks.mitigation: The default SimpleKeyGenerator keys the filtered finder on (specialty, pageable), distinct from findAll()'s EMPTY key and findAll(Pageable)'s pageable key, so no collision. Route blank/absent to the existing findAll methods so their cached unfiltered entries are reused unchanged.

risks.risk: The owner-list template does NOT carry its lastName across page links (verified in ownersList.html) — copying it verbatim would drop the specialty on paging and violate REQ-VET-001's 'keeps the narrowing applied'
risks.mitigation: vetList.html must append the model's specialty value to every page/first/prev/next/last link; do not clone the owner template's pagination as-is.

risks.risk: Paging over a ManyToMany join could distort the page count with duplicate rows
risks.mitigation: specialties is a Set and the filter names one specialty, so each matching vet appears once; still confirm total-count reflects distinct vets under the H2 test.

notes: Verdict minor: no ADR beyond the already-written adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md — the decision here is applying an existing pattern, not a hard-to-reverse architectural choice. The empty-result-is-HTTP-200 and blank-as-absent behaviors are product rules already fixed in the PRD and non-goal ADR. Durable write this dispatch: added the non-goal ADR index row to docs/adr/README.md (assigned to system-design-expert; outside product-requirements-expert scope). Deferred to doc-sync post-implementation, NOT written now because they describe implemented state: wire REQ-VET-003 into the Implements column for VetController / VetRepository / Vets and the /vets route, and revise the 'machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement' row in system-design Known Defects since REQ-VET-003 now gives that route a requirement. Security/reliability: read-only GET, no new trust boundary; the echoed specialty value is Thymeleaf-escaped and the derived query keeps it parameterized (no SQLi); no autofix records to audit this dispatch.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: specialty flows only into Spring Data derived finders (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) — bound-parameter queries, no SQLi surface

pagination links use Thymeleaf URL-expression param syntax @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}: query-param values are URL-encoded and th:href output HTML-attribute-escaped, so the reflected specialty cannot break out for XSS

new finders are not @Cacheable (only @Transactional readOnly); attacker-controlled specialty values never enter the vets cache key-space, so no cache poisoning or unbounded-cache-growth path; blank/absent routes to the existing cached findAll unchanged
read-only public GET over already-public vet/specialty data — no trust boundary or authz change; blank/all-spaces normalized to absent before reaching the query

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: REQ-VET-003 acceptance criterion 'given a blank or all-spaces narrowing, when the machine-readable directory is requested, then it behaves as though no narrowing were given' has no test. blankSpecialtyIsTreatedAsNoNarrowing covers only the HTML surface (/vets.html); the JSON surface (/vets) is untested for this case. The controller may or may not normalise the parameter consistently between both surfaces — the gap leaves a defect path open.

New test methods do not follow the BDD naming school required for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward (testing-principles.md § Test Naming: the{Subject}Should{Outcome}). Names like htmlDirectoryNarrowedToSpecialtyListsOnlyMatchingVets, unmatchedSpecialtyYieldsEmptyDirectoryWithNormalResponse, blankSpecialtyIsTreatedAsNoNarrowing, laterPageOfFilteredDirectoryKeepsNarrowing, machineReadableDirectoryNarrowedToSpecialtyReturnsOnlyMatchingVets, machineReadableUnmatchedSpecialtyReturnsEmptyDirectory describe what the system does rather than stating what must be true. Each should be renamed to the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} form, e.g. theHtmlDirectoryNarrowedToSpecialtyShouldListOnlyMatchingVets.
findings.fix: Rename each new test method to follow the{Subject}Should{Outcome}: theHtmlDirectoryNarrowedToSpecialtyShouldListOnlyMatchingVets, theUnmatchedSpecialtyShouldYieldEmptyDirectoryWithNormalResponse, theBlankSpecialtyShouldBeTreatedAsNoNarrowing, theLaterPageOfFilteredDirectoryShouldKeepNarrowing, theMachineReadableDirectoryNarrowedToSpecialtyShouldReturnOnlyMatchingVets, theMachineReadableUnmatchedSpecialtyShouldReturnEmptyDirectory.

findings.description: New test methods in ClinicServiceTests also do not follow the BDD naming school: shouldFindVetsBySpecialtyWholeNameCaseInsensitively, shouldNotMatchSpecialtyByPrefix, shouldReturnNoVetsForUnheldSpecialty start with 'should' but omit the 'the{Subject}' prefix. They should follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} form.

Narration comment inside laterPageOfFilteredDirectoryKeepsNarrowing violates testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure ('never add prose that restates what the code already says'). The comment 'six matches over a page size of five yields a second page whose links must carry the narrowing' narrates the intent already readable from the PageRequest.of(0, 5) and the 6-total constructor argument.

author: change-grader
summary: filter both vet directory surfaces by an optional specialty query parameter

blast_radius.note: Contained to the vet feature: two prod Java files plus one template in the vet package, two test files, and three docs; two prod modules, no sensitive paths, 191 tracked insertions. Reach is narrow and read-only (public GET over already-public vet data).

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk. normalizeSpecialty returns null on null/blank/all-spaces and strips otherwise; both handlers branch null to findAll, else to findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, with no inverted conditional or off-by-one. The template swap from the old string-concatenated page link to the Thymeleaf URL builder that appends specialty is a correct hardening, not a hidden behavior change; a null specialty is omitted from the link.

test_adequacy.note: Tests assert real outcomes, not the implementation. H2 repository tests prove whole-name case-insensitivity (radiology and RADIOLOGY both size 2), prefix non-match (rad returns empty), and unheld-empty; controller tests cover filtered, unmatched, and blank on both HTML and JSON surfaces and assert the pagination link carries specialty=radiology. The round-1 critical JSON-blank gap was closed and re-verified.

reviewer_hedging.note: Final round is a clean unanimous approval from all four reviewers with empty findings. The round-1 critical (untested JSON blank-narrowing) and the code-quality truncation were resolved and explicitly re-verified in round 2; the design-block was minor with no revisions. No lingering caveats or escalate tags remain.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, consultations, and build retries. The diff matches the triaged surface exactly: optional specialty on both surfaces, one shared matcher, the parameter carried on every page link, URL-contract-only. The REQ-VET-001 plus REQ-VET-003 span is the designed scope, not a wander; the three product-owner decisions are recorded in docs.
